title: Introduce tenant priority slices and eviction reserve orchestrator
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally face tight contention when many tenants attempt short bursts simultaneously which amplifies tail latency and increases preemptions. This PR implements a lightweight tenant priority slicing primitive plus an eviction-reserve orchestrator that preserves low-latency guarantees for higher-priority tenants while limiting global churn. The change introduces a coordinated allocator that assigns each tenant a small, elastic 'slice' of headroom that grows with recent stable throughput and can be temporarily topped up from a bounded eviction reserve pool during surges. The reserve is funded by reclaimed soft capacity and soft-degraded reservations and decays over a configurable window. Design highlights: 1) Priority slices are configured per-tenant via the existing DedicatedConfig API with two new fields: priority_level (int) and slice_target_tokens_per_sec (float). 2) The orchestrator runs inside the fleet controller loop and maintains three logical buckets: committed capacity, slice headroom, and eviction reserve. 3) When demand exceeds slices, the orchestrator allocates reserve credits using a proportional scoring function that prefers higher priority tenants and favors tenants with recent successful rollbacks from reserve. 4) Eviction-reserve allocations are timeboxed, and the orchestrator emits explicit eviction-reserve events to the audit log so customer billing/chargeback can reconcile short-term reserve usage. 5) Built-in safety: a global reserve cap, per-tenant max-reserve, and fast-eviction heuristics ensure no tenant can monopolize reserve for more than the configured decay window. Implementation summary: - scheduler/allocator/priority_slices.go: core allocation logic and unit-tested scoring function (600 additions). - controller/fleet/orchestrator.go: integration into fleet controller loop, reserve state machine, metrics hooks. - api/dedicated_types.go: adds two new config fields and validation with backwards compatibility. - charts/dedicated/values.yaml: feature flag toggle and default knobs for reserve size and decay window. - telemetry/metrics.go: new time-series metrics: dedicated.slice_allocated_tokens, dedicated.reserve_granted_tokens, dedicated.reserve_evictions, dedicated.slice_utilization_percent, and a histogram dedicated.reserve_latency_seconds. - cli/fleetctl: expose a new `fleetctl reserve-status` command to inspect live reserve state and per-tenant slices. Rollout plan: feature disabled by default; gate behind a feature-flag (DEDICATED_PRIORITY_SLICES) and a chart toggle. We will enable in Canary fleet for two weeks with telemetry dashboards in Redwood Console (new default dashboard saved under Dedicated > PrioritySlices). Backout plan: feature flag off will short-circuit orchestrator and reconcile all reserve allocations; a follow-up hotfix branch contains a migration that drains reserve quickly if users prefer immediate rollback. Related: ENG-2147 (autoscaler fairness gaps), ENG-2210 (tenant preemption incidents), SUP-4321 (customer escalation during incident 2025-01-11).

review_comments: Evan Jacobs: Nice work; please add throttling to the CLI command to avoid load on large clusters. Also gate the metrics emission behind the feature flag to avoid cardinality during rollout.
Priya Menon (author): Added token-bucket throttle to fleetctl reserve-status and gated metrics behind DEDICATED_PRIORITY_SLICES. See commit 2b9f8d4.
Marta López: Scoring function looks good, but we should cap per-tenant reserve to avoid noisy neighbors. Add a test that simulates burst storms from many tenants.
Priya Menon (author): Added per-tenant max-reserve and a synthetic storm test in tests/integration/priority_slices_e2e_test.go.
Connor Reed: CI failed on race; found a data-race in orchestrator state transition. Suggest using controller-runtime's workqueue to serialize state writes.
Priya Menon (author): Addressed by synchronizing reserve state updates and adding a dedicated worker; re-ran CI and race disappears (see commit 2b9f8d4).

release_notes: Add tenant priority slices and eviction reserve orchestrator; feature gated behind DEDICATED_PRIORITY_SLICES. New telemetry metrics and a CLI command to inspect reserve state. Backwards compatible by default (feature off).
notes_for_ops: Enable feature on canary fleet only. Recommended default knobs: global_reserve_tokens: 500000, reserve_decay_window_seconds: 600, per_tenant_max_reserve_tokens: 20000. Monitor dedicated.reserve_evictions and dedicated.slice_utilization_percent for 48h before broad rollout.
